hints.title: Perimeter Escapability Obstacle
hints.text: Capturing all 'O' regions entirely surrounded by 'X' by checking every interior cell forward is tricky because regions can curve to the border. How can reversing perspective and starting from perimeter 'O' cells solve this?

hints.title: Boundary Reachability Invariant
hints.text: Any 'O' connected directly or indirectly to the perimeter borders can never be surrounded. All other 'O' cells are completely surrounded and must flip to 'X'.

hints.title: Three-Phase Border Mark Procedure
hints.text: Phase 1: Mark all border 'O' cells and their connected 'O' neighbors with temporary character 'E'. Phase 2: Iterate through all cells; flip remaining 'O' to 'X'. Phase 3: Restore 'E' cells back to 'O'.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Every cell is visited a constant number of times with recursion stack bounded by M * N.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching inward from interior 'O' cells requires complex path backtrack to confirm border isolation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place temporary character marking requires zero auxiliary matrices.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Boundary-first traversal concept to simplify surrounded region identification.
